brief.situation: 16:00 in the NICU. You are the bedside nurse for Baby Nguyen, a stable 30-week infant who needs a non-urgent PICC line placed this evening. The parents speak Vietnamese and limited English. The fellow wants to get consent now using the infant's 12-year-old sister, who speaks English, so the line can go in before the night shift, and asks you to sign as witness. Work out what is being asked, advocate for the infant and family, and keep the working relationship where you can.
handover: Your professional code makes the patient your primary commitment and asks you to advocate for the rights, health and safety of the people in your care, including their family's right to understand.

Hospital policy: qualified medical interpreters (in person, video or phone) are available around the clock at no cost; minors and family members do not interpret except in an emergency; ethics concerns can go to the charge nurse and the ethics consult service.
howItWorks: Choose what to ask or say. Each exchange takes a few minutes of the conversation; Dr. Patel answers at once, and the next choice waits for the exchange to finish.
The screen shows Dr. Patel, how hard she is pushing, your working relationship, what you know so far, and your note.
When the conversation ends you write your note and explain your reasoning.

reflection.question: For your note: what the ethical concern was, how you advocated for the infant and family, and how you worked with the fellow.

parts.label: The concern
parts.criteria: Names that consent through a 12-year-old is not informed consent: a minor interpreter is not allowed except in an emergency, the child doesn't know the terms, and the parents' right to understand the risks is the infant's protection.
parts.modelAnswer: Using the 12-year-old means the parents can't really give informed consent. It isn't an emergency, she doesn't know the words, and they have a right to hear the risks in their language.

parts.label: Ask, then act
parts.criteria: Asks how urgent the line is and whether the interpreter was tried before answering; declines and offers a route that meets the fellow's goal (the video interpreter now).
parts.modelAnswer: I asked whether it was urgent and whether the interpreter was tried, then offered to bring the video cart so it still gets done tonight.

parts.label: The relationship and the channel
parts.criteria: Acknowledges the fellow's workload; involves the charge nurse, not threats or posts; writes a factual note.
parts.modelAnswer: I acknowledged her evening, got the charge nurse to cover, and documented the consent conversation.

scoring.modelReasoning: Advocacy means acting for the infant through the family who decides for him. Outside an emergency, a minor child must not interpret, and qualified language assistance must be offered free of charge. Ask first: the line is not urgent and the video interpreter is minutes away. Acknowledge the fellow's workload, decline to witness consent through the sister, bring the interpreter now so the line still goes in tonight, keep the risks in the conversation, involve the charge nurse rather than threats or posts, and document.
